key_insight: Neptuna introduces the first large-scale benchmark for shock-driven compressible multiphase flows and shows that no single surrogate model or loss wins across all cases, but composite losses and SoftAdapt improve interface and spectral fidelity.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives researchers a realistic testbed for building and comparing machine learning surrogates for bubble collapse and droplet breakup in compressible multiphase systems.
method: Benchmarking on 2.4 TB of 2D and 3D high-fidelity datasets for shock-induced bubble collapse and droplet breakup
Comparison of convolutional, spectral, transformer-based, and pre-trained PDE foundation models
Training with MSE plus Sobolev, interface-aware, and structure-aware losses, with SoftAdapt and GradNorm for adaptive balancing
evidence_signal: The study evaluates models with pointwise, spectral, feature-focused, structural, and physics-informed metrics across large-scale 2D and 3D datasets.
watch_item: Results appear dataset- and metric-dependent, so improvements from composite losses or adaptive weighting may not transfer uniformly to all multiphase flow scenarios.
paper_title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows
